title: D1 feel pass: cascade motion must read smooth+natural at 1x — visual tuning loop
description: Greg: 'incredibly important that it feels smooth and natural, test it alot.' Beyond the logic gate: demo harness (DinoDigger/Demo/Dig menu: enter dig, trigger single-fall / column-collapse / geode-cascade patterns, slow-mo toggle), motion constants lifted to GameConfig (fall accel/ease, per-row duration, stagger, squash amplitude, bounce recovery, dust size/count), then iterative visual review of captured frame sequences at timeScale 1 and 0.25 until falls read weighty-but-bouncy toy-box, no pops/teleports/hitches. Multiple observed cascades of each pattern per round.
notes: Orchestrator feel review (slow-mo capture frames, 0.25x): cascade motion coherent — no teleports/overlaps, staggered falls visible, landing cracks propagate, peeks ride their tiles, coin uncovered cleanly in crumbled pocket, geode reads special vs crystals, site-roller cluster stable per no-new-contact rule. Verdict: PASS for mechanics+motion. Tuning note for Greg's live pass: dust per landing reads sparse in stills — all motion is now live-tunable GameConfig sliders (DigDust*, DigFall*, DigSquash*) + DinoDigger/Demo/Dig menu for A/B. Final say = Greg by hand.
close_reason:
Feel harness landed: every cascade/toy motion number is now a tunable GameConfig field, and there is a menu to drive the dig by eye.

CONFIG (new [Header] blocks in GameConfig, all with tooltips, defaults == the shipped values): Dig cascade feel — DigFallRowSeconds 0.07, DigFallMinSeconds 0.05, DigFallMaxSeconds 0.28, DigFallStaggerSeconds 0.05, DigFallStaggerMaxSeconds 0.25, DigFallEase (new FallEase enum: Accelerate/Linear/EaseOut/EaseInOut), DigSquashAmplitude 0.18, DigSquashRecoverSeconds 0.22, DigDustPerLanding 4, DigLandingThumpGapSeconds 0.08. Dig toys — DigCrystalPopRingSeconds 0.03, DigCrystalPopFadeSeconds 0.14, DigCrystalSparkleCount 12, DigCrystalCoinBase 1, DigCrystalCoinMax 12, DigGeodeFuseSeconds 0.4, DigGeodeShakeAmplitude 0.09, DigGeodeShakeSeconds 0.28, DigGeodeDustCount 18, DigPotCoinMin 5, DigPotCoinMax 8, DigPotCoinArcSeconds 0.55, DigPotCoinCollectSeconds 1.0. Site generation — DigCrystalSiteChance 0.65, DigCrystalClusterCount 2, DigCrystalClusterMin/Max 3/6, DigGeodeChance 0.3, DigPotChance 0.35.

LIVE TUNING: the runtime reads these on every USE and never caches them at build time — DigFallSeconds(drop)/DigFallStagger(order)/DigFallCurve(u) are called per mover per frame in SettlePass and DirtTile.FallTo, and DirtTile.Squash reads amplitude/recovery at impact. So a slider dragged in play mode retunes the very next tile that falls (FallEase even re-curves falls already in the air). All helpers clamp, so a silly inspector value looks silly but can never stall a tile or divide by zero. The old cascade consts survive only as no-config fallbacks.

MENU (new Assets/Scripts/Editor/DemoDigMenu.cs, play-mode-guarded and null-tolerant like DemoTownMenu): DinoDigger/Demo/Dig/ — Enter First Dig (nearest active mound via the public GameManager.EnterDig, no cross-island commute), Spawn Crystal Cluster (2x2, colour rotates per click), Spawn Boom Geode, Spawn Pinata Pot, Trigger Column Collapse, Slow Motion 0.25x, Normal Speed, plus Log Dig Framing which prints the dig root, DigCenter and ortho size for capture framing. Editor scripts cannot see internal Test* hooks, so DigModeController gained a small PUBLIC Demo* surface (DemoSpawnCrystalCluster / DemoSpawnGeode / DemoSpawnPot / DemoCollapseColumn / DigRootPosition) that no-ops outside an open site.

CAPTURE FRAMING: dig root is at world (1000, 0, 0) (SceneBuilder.DigRootPos); the camera frames DigCenter = (1000, -1.5, 0) at 5 rows, ortho size GameConfig.DigOrthoSize 4.2 — visible y approx [-5.7, +2.7], x approx +-6.7 at 16:10.

Camera nudge for the geode goes through CameraFollow.ShakeDig, which shakes around the dig framing the rig already owns and refuses to run mid-transition — no live-transform snapshots, and it always lands back on the exact framing.

NOT done here (deliberately, this agent was files-only): the iterative by-eye review of captured frame sequences at 1x and 0.25x. The harness for it is in place; the review itself is the orchestrator's capture loop.

title: D1b: Crystal color-pops, boom geodes, pinata pots
description: Crystal tiles (theme-tinted, 3 colors): tap pops the whole connected same-color blob (flood fill), bigger blob = bigger confetti + coin bonus; auto-pop when a fall brings same-color crystals into contact. Boom geode: rare tile clearing 3x3 with soft whumph + giggle, feeds cascades. Pinata pot: crackable pot spraying a fountain of bouncing coins. All zero-fail, all bonus. Cases: CrystalPopFloodFill, BoomChainsResolve, PinataPotPays. Depends on D1a engine.
close_reason:
Dig toys shipped as DirtTile KINDS (Config/GameEnums.DigTileKind: Dirt/Crystal/Geode/Pot), so all three fall, crack and clear through the existing gravity chokepoint with zero special cases inside the cascade engine.

CRYSTALS: tap pops the whole 4-way connected same-colour blob (BFS flood fill, ring depths). Logic is SYNCHRONOUS (whole blob cleared + one SettleGrid on the tapped frame, like the engine's own fall logic) while the LOOK ripples outward at DigCrystalPopRingSeconds/ring via DirtTile.ForceBreak(visualDelay) + per-crystal sparkle burst. Pays DigCrystalCoinBase per crystal (clamped by DigCrystalCoinMax) through SpawnRewardPickup. Crystals are exempt from landing cracks (1-hardness would shatter under falling dirt for no coins).

AUTO-POP: rides the settle loop as ONE extra pass. SettleGrid snapshots same-colour crystal contacts (instance-id pair keys) before the first pass; when compaction goes quiet, blobs containing a NEW contact pop, and only if something popped does the loop go round again. One auto-pop pass per settle, inside the existing MaxSettlePasses cap — so a site-generated cluster riding a column down is never evaporated, but a crystal landing beside its colour chains for free.

BOOM GEODE: DirtTile.Damage intercepts kind Geode and ARMS instead of taking the hit, so tap / landing crack / crew clear all light the same fuse. DigGeodeFuseSeconds of sparkle anticipation (generation-guarded), then a 3x3 top-down clear from its CURRENT row/col (it may have fallen mid-fuse), dust ring, tiny camera nudge (GameManager.DigShakeCamera -> CameraFollow.ShakeDig, shaking around the owned dig framing, never a live snapshot), Roar as the whumph/giggle audio hook, one shared settle. A crystal caught in the 3x3 takes its whole blob with it.

PINATA POT: hardness 2, pinata_pot_cracked on the crack state. Breaking it ANY way (two taps, crew clear, or a falling rock — pots are deliberately NOT exempt from landing cracks) sprays DigPotCoinMin..Max coins that arc, bounce, shine and auto-collect; the pit visual and the banked pickup are separate so spray count and wallet can never disagree.

Buried-item layer stays independent: PlaceDigToys runs before PlaceItems/PlaceSurprisePocket and both skip non-dirt cells, so a toy cell never also hides loot or the pocket.

ART: GeneratedArtImporter gained a dig category — crystals/geode/pot sized by their LARGER dimension to DirtTargetH (ConfigureCellFit) so every toy fits the 1x1 grid cell whatever its aspect; dust_thump imports as a particle. Wired to new typed PlaceholderLibrary fields (CrystalSprites[3], BoomGeode, PinataPot, PinataPotCracked, DustPuff), no reflection. Missing art degrades to a tinted dirt sprite rather than a blank cell.

TESTS (+3, suite 64 -> 67): CrystalPopFloodFill (hand-built blob via TestSetCrystal, one tap pops all 4, a touching odd colour survives, coins exact, board settled + idempotent), BoomChainsResolve (geode beside a blob: fuse then 3x3 chaining into the blob, settle under cap, no floaters, zero console errors, site still tappable), PinataPotPays (crack pays nothing, break pays exactly what it sprayed). New TestSuppressToys static + TestSetCrystal/Geode/Pot + TestBlobSizeAt/TestLastPotCoins/TestGeodeBooms/TestAutoPops hooks; no reflection, counter-driven, no wall clock.

Verified: Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-Editor both compile clean (csc against the project's own csproj reference set); no Unity/editor run from this agent.

title: D1a: Gravity cascade engine — tiles fall, crack, settle; superpowers rewired
description: Core physics: when tiles clear, tiles above fall column-wise; falls crack tiles they land on (1 hardness tick), reveal peeks, and trigger settle re-checks. Deterministic settle loop with generation guard (geode lesson: no deferred callback may cross a site close/open). Buddy superpowers (T-Rex clear, Trike column, geode chain) route through the same engine. Cases: TilesFallAndSettle, CascadeNeverWedges. Feel: falls are chunky (slight bounce, dust puff per landing), never block taps.
notes:
Gravity cascade engine landed (files only; no Unity run/commit).

ENGINE (DigModeController): ClearTile (vacate cell + collect) -> SettleGrid (repeat SettlePass until a pass moves nothing) -> SettlePass (per column, bottom-up compaction to the lowest free cell; record faller->victim landings; then one Damage() tick per landing; a tick that crumbles a victim re-enters ClearTile and the next pass turns the hole into more falling). Logic is fully SYNCHRONOUS; only travel is tweened (0.05s/tile stagger, 0.07s/row, capped 0.28s). Cap MaxSettlePasses=64 with Debug.LogError; true bound ~1+rows*cols. Generation-guarded every pass + in the landing FX callback.

DECISION: items fall WITH their tile (_buried is keyed by tile reference, the peek is a child renderer) - a cell-pinned item would glow through a different tile than the one hiding it.

POCKET INTEGRITY: landing ticks SKIP the surprise tile (must be discovered, never squashed); breadcrumb extended with the 'cascade landing' cause.

REWIRED: player bite + T-Rex adjacent now vacate first and share ONE SettleGrid per bite; Trike column + geode chain + TestClearSurpriseTile route through ClearTileFully -> TileCleared. OnTileTapped drops taps on a falling tile (input never blocked).

TESTS: TilesFallAndSettle + CascadeNeverWedges registered (64 cases). Audit fixes: reference-captured neighbour damage sums (BigDinoHelps, BuddyDigCrew), !IsFalling tap pacing (TapTileUntilDestroyed, FindPlainTile, DirtTileDamage, BuddyDigCrew loops), column hardness pinning where a 1-tap tile would let a landing crack chain (SurprisePocket Giggle section).
close_reason: Gravity cascade engine implemented: synchronous settle loop (compaction + landing cracks + chained falls) with a 64-pass loud cap, staggered chunky fall/squash/dust visuals, taps never blocked, all clearing paths (bite, T-Rex adjacent, Trike column, geode chain) rewired through one chokepoint, items fall with their tile, surprise pocket exempt from landing cracks. Cases TilesFallAndSettle + CascadeNeverWedges added; existing dig cases audited and de-flaked for a moving grid. Files written only - suite not run (no Unity per task rules).

title: BUG: diagonal facings wrong (NW shows SE; SE shows SW) for dinos AND backhoe
description: User screenshots: purple stego faces SE while moving NW (180 flip); player+dinos face SW when moving SE (adjacent swap). Cardinals are correct (tests cover them) — DIAGONAL mapping is broken somewhere: Direction8 sector->Dir8 for diagonals, importer's mirrored-sprite assignment (SW/W/NW from SE/E/NE), or array index order. Investigate against actual sprite files; fix; EXTEND FacingCorrectness to all 8 directions (diagonal legs) so this can never regress.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Greg Back
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (art data, not code). Each non-front facing is produced INDEPENDENTLY by
img2img-rotating the front (S) reference with an AMBIGUOUS, character-relative prompt in
Tools/generate_sprites.py ("...we see its front AND its RIGHT side"). The image model
read "its right side" inconsistently -- often as the character's ANATOMICAL right, which
lands on SCREEN-LEFT -- so a subset of generated facings came out horizontally MIRRORED
vs the compass name in their filename. Because the slicer builds the left set (SW/W/NW)
by flipping the right set (SE/E/NE), a mirrored source silently swaps the whole pair.

This is NOT a math bug. Verified: Direction8.FromVector maps diagonals correctly
((1,-1)->SE, (-1,1)->NW, (1,1)->NE, (-1,-1)->SW), the slicer's SE->SW/E->W/NE->NW mirror
is geometrically correct, and SW/W/NW PNGs are EXACT pixel-mirrors of SE/E/NE (meanAbsDiff
0.00 for all actors). The FacingCorrectness test passed on diagonals-would-have-passed
because it only checks Dir8-index<->array-slot consistency, which was always correct -- it
has no way to SEE which way the art points. That is why the defect was invisible to tests.

The mislabeling is PER-(actor,facing), NOT a uniform swap. Evidence from the unambiguous
sprites (backhoe loader/cab-face; dino snouts/beaks/frills), eyeballed at high resolution:
  backhoe_SE  -> faces SW (face+loader point down-LEFT)      [SWAP]
  backhoe_NE  -> faces NW (loader up-left, taillight to cam) [SWAP]
  triceratops_SE -> faces SW (beak points LEFT)              [SWAP]
  triceratops_NE -> faces NE (beak points RIGHT)             [CORRECT]  <- same actor, opposite!
  trex_SE / spinosaurus_SE / brachiosaurus_SE / velociraptor_SE / parasaurolophus_SE
              -> faces SE (snout RIGHT)                       [CORRECT]
  stegosaurus_SE -> faces SW (snout LEFT)                    [SWAP]
  ankylosaurus_E/SE/NE -> all face LEFT                       [SWAP] (whole actor mirrored;
              even the E cardinal profile is flipped)

FIX (two layers, no regeneration required):
1) GeneratedArtImporter.cs -- added a per-actor facing-correction table (FlippedFacingPairs)
   + AdultSuffix(). Because W/SW/NW are exact mirrors of E/SE/NE, the correctly-oriented
   sprite for a mirrored facing ALREADY EXISTS as its partner file, so a flipped slot is
   corrected by loading the partner (a per-actor compass horizontal pair-swap). Only
   HIGH-CONFIDENCE flips are listed so the fix can NEVER regress an already-correct actor:
     backhoe {SE,NE}, triceratops {SE}, stegosaurus {SE}, ankylosaurus {E,SE,NE}.
   Applied to adult idle + adult strides + backhoe rolls (they inherit each facing's
   handedness via the same suffix path -- covers every array the importer fills for those
   actors). Verified visually: post-fix, all 8 backhoe slots face their compass label and
   the stego SE/SW pair is corrected.
2) Tools/generate_sprites.py -- rewrote ROTATE to be SCREEN-relative and unambiguous
   (head/front points to the frame's right, rotation pinned toward the frame RIGHT) plus a
   NO_MIRROR clause, and documented that the slicer MIRROR step is correct but depends on
   source orientation. This is the permanent root-cause fix; regenerating with it yields a
   consistent set, after which the importer table should be emptied.

TESTS: Case_FacingCorrectness extended from 4 cardinals to all 8 headings. Added
FindClearStraightTarget (arbitrary heading + CORRIDOR line-of-sight, so diagonal legs
drive straight instead of staircasing) and RelocateForEightWay/RankEightWay (seek open
ground covering both axes AND both diagonal hands). Coverage now requires both axes + >=2
diagonals. Added DinoDiagonalSpotCheck: a follower dino must index a diagonal facing to the
right slot (idle or either stride phase). NOTE documented in-test: this guards the Dir8
sector math + array indexing only -- it cannot detect art-orientation flips.

RESIDUAL / FOLLOW-UP (not a regression -- these keep current behavior, just not yet
corrected): baby/kid stage sets are SEPARATE generations and were NOT audited; a few adult
NE rear-views (brachiosaurus, pteranodon, parasaurolophus) and pteranodon_SE were too
ambiguous to classify at high confidence and were left untouched. The clean permanent fix
for all of these is to regenerate with the corrected prompt (Tools/generate_sprites.py) and
then empty the importer's FlippedFacingPairs table.

title: BUG: duplicate species eggs (2 T-Rex) — uniqueness race
description: User dug 2 T-Rex eggs. Root cause hypothesis: TryRollUnownedEggSpecies checks OWNED (hatched) dinos only — multiple eggs rolled before the first HATCHES can all pick the same species. Fix: reserve species when the egg DugItemInfo is created (pending set: buried eggs + spilled unhatched eggs), release on hatch/destroy; roll excludes owned+pending. Test: dig two egg batches without hatching -> species differ; also UniqueDinoNoDupes extension.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Greg Back
comments.text:
FIXED — duplicate-egg-species race (2 T-Rex).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): TryRollUnownedEggSpecies excluded only OWNED = HATCHED
species (OwnedEggSpecies iterates _dinos, the live DinoControllers). An egg that
was dug but not yet hatched is a live ItemPickup, never in _dinos. FinishDig
resolves the WHOLE batch (GameManager.cs loop calling ResolveDugItem) BEFORE any
pickup spawns/hatches, so two eggs in one batch both saw the same "owned" set and
Random.Range could pick the same unowned species -> 2 T-Rex. Same hole across two
quick digs and for spilled-but-un-hatched eggs.

FIX — pending-species reservation set in GameManager:
- Dictionary<DinoType,int> _reservedEggSpecies (ref-counted, defence in depth).
- TryRollUnownedEggSpecies now excludes OWNED *and* RESERVED species.
- ResolveDugItem RESERVES the species the instant an egg is finalized (after the
  unique re-roll), so a second egg in the same batch / a later dig cannot pick it.
- No-species-remaining fallback: if EggSpeciesAllOwned() (nerf active) -> shard
  (else treasure), else -> FRUIT. Rationale: shards must never drop before every
  egg species is owned, so a batch that merely exhausts the *reserved* pool spills
  fruit rather than leaking an early shard.

RELEASE POINTS:
- HatchEgg: releases the reservation and takes ownership (SpawnDino) in one
  synchronous step — no gap for a duplicate. Direct HatchEgg (no pickup) = no-op.
- ItemPickup.OnDestroy: releases for an egg destroyed WITHOUT hatching (dig
  re-entry, reset); guarded with _hatched flag + !Application.isPlaying so
  play-mode-exit / domain-reload teardown is a safe no-op.
- TestReset: _reservedEggSpecies.Clear().

AUDIT of every egg-DugItemInfo path: FinishDig->ResolveDugItem (reserves) OK;
SpawnRewardPickup now routes egg type through ResolveDugItem (duck reward is only
fruit/treasure today, but the gate is closed); DropTreeFruit makes Fruit only (no
eggs) OK; TestSpawnItem reserves egg species for the pickup lifetime. PEEK during
digging is cosmetic (site-roll tint) and unchanged — two buried eggs at ONE site
now DO get distinct species because FinishDig re-rolls each through the reserving
ResolveDugItem.

TESTS (IntegrationTestCases.Case_UniqueDinoNoDupes extended): resolve a 6-egg
batch with nothing owned -> assert 4 DISTINCT egg species + 2 fruit fallbacks + 0
shard/treasure leak; assert 4 reservations held; reset; assert reservations
cleared; then the original partial/full owned-exclusion assertions. New hooks:
TestResolveDugBatch (mirrors FinishDig, keeps reservations), TestReservedEggSpeciesCount.
TestRollDugItem now releases the egg it samples so the sampling distribution stays
stationary (keeps existing UniqueDinoNoDupes/ShardDropRate/ShardHatchCeremony green).
FeedAndGrow/EggHatch spawn via TestSpawnItem: fruit un-affected; the egg reserves
then releases on hatch.

FILES: Assets/Scripts/Core/GameManager.cs, Assets/Scripts/Overworld/ItemPickup.cs,
Assets/Scripts/Testing/IntegrationTestCases.cs. (Not compiled/run here — no Unity
MCP; rerun DinoDigger/Run Integration Tests to verify.)

title: ENV integration: overlay layers + prop swaps in engine
description: Wire the env set: tilemap overlay layers (base mottle variants, transition strips, decal scatter with the grammar), importer env category, SceneBuilder swaps for trees/rocks/bridges/fences/mounds, WebGL texture budget check (+~0.5MB target), FacingCorrectness-class regression watch (env must not affect walkability/colliders). Pilot the meadow region first, then whole island. All existing cases must stay green (tree-shake, rock-smash, mound taps hit the SAME colliders).
close_reason:
ENV set wired into the engine. 117 sprites in Assets/Art/Generated/env/ now paint the island.

DESIGN - the one constraint that shaped everything: GameManager routes tree/rock taps by
comparing the obstacle tile against lib.TreeTile / lib.RockTile (and BrachioTreeShake /
AnkyRockSmash find their targets the same way). So props are restyled IN PLACE - the Tile
ASSET's sprite is re-pointed, the Tile REFERENCE never changes. Zero risk to the tap
contract, zero collider retuning, and already-painted scenes stay valid.

IMPORTER (GeneratedArtImporter, new ENV section)
  World size is the contract, not PPU: each asset stores a TARGET WORLD WIDTH and the
  importer derives PPU = sourceWidthPx / worldWidth, so a re-bake at a new resolution keeps
  the footprint instead of resizing the island. Reproduces c7m's mapping exactly -
  ground/bridge/mound/tree/rock 256px -> PPU 256, nest -> 200, fence -> 100.
  Pivots are CENTER, not bottom-center: every prop replaced here is either a tilemap tile
  (a bottom pivot would shift the whole island half a cell) or a center-pivoted
  SpriteRenderer prop (DigMound sits centered on its collider; the nest bowl at local zero;
  Kenney fence pieces are center-pivoted and SceneBuilder offsets by half-height).
  Creates 107 Tile assets in env/Tiles/ (colliderType None) and fills typed library slots.
  Skips the 1024^2 pipeline masters (plate_*) and the review sheets by design.

LIBRARY (new Config/EnvDressing.cs + PlaceholderLibrary ENV block)
  [Serializable] EnvTileSet (TileBase[] variants + hashed Variant(cell,salt) + Contains) and
  EnvEdgeSet (ByMask[16], keyed by the baked art's own 4-bit neighbour mask: bit0 -Y,
  bit1 +X, bit2 +Y, bit3 -X). Fields: GrassTiles/PathTiles/WaterTiles/BedTiles,
  GrassPathEdges/GrassWaterEdges/GrassBedEdges, four decal buckets, BridgeTiles, tree/rock/
  bridge sprite arrays, TreeShakeSprite, FenceAlongX/Y. GroundTileFor() and DecalTileFor()
  are the single source of truth, shared by the painter and the verifier so they cannot drift.

SCENEBUILDER
  Variants: deterministic per cell via a mixed integer hash of (x,y,salt) - no System.Random
  anywhere, so a rebuild reproduces the island exactly. Verified distribution: all 16 grass
  variants used, 131-167 cells each over 2304, no row/column striping.
  Edges: a grass cell computes the mask of neighbours sharing ONE foreign biome (first in bit
  order wins; the art has no three-way transitions) and paints edge_grass_<other>_<mask>.
  Bridges read as water to their grass neighbours, matching the art's own reference composer.
  Bed: the Berry Patch plot ('A') finally gets the tilled garden-bed ground plus a grass->bed
  rim - still ordinary walkable ground, identical to grass for every query.
  Decals: new "Decals" Tilemap at sortingOrder 2 (above ground/water 0/1, below obstacles 5,
  mounds 8, fences 9, actors 12/15). Grammar-bucketed per rule 4 - ferns/moss/clover only on
  grass, footprints/pebbles on path, lilies on water, warm stones a rare path accent.
  Densities in GameConfig's new append-only ENV region (0.20/0.34/0.22, accent 0.12; measured
  ~0.195/0.332/0.214 in simulation). Skips prop cells, bridge decks, the town district, the
  garden plot, every mound cell and the start cell, so a decal can never sit under a tap
  target.
  Props: fence pieces now come from the library (canvas-compatible Kenney drop-ins, same
  256x512 canvas + alpha bbox, so the existing scale-to-cell-width maths lands them
  identically); mound + nest sprites swap through existing library slots so DigMound,
  BerrySprout, the machine blob fallback and NestController all pick them up with no code
  change.

WEBGL - verified, no change needed: the override sweep searches "Assets/Art" recursively, so
all 117 env textures already get the 256px crunched treatment (and every shipped env PNG is
authored <=256px, so it costs no resolution). Added an EnvDir constant + an explicit env count
in the log line so the coverage is reported rather than assumed.

FALLBACKS - every slot null-tolerant. No env art (or GameConfig.EnvDressingEnabled off) and
SceneBuilder paints the exact flat tiles it painted before; a half-imported set falls back
slot by slot. The game can never regress below today.

TESTS - new case EnvDressingApplied (IntegrationTestCasesEnv.cs; IntegrationTestCases.cs
touched for exactly one registration line). Asserts: >1 distinct grass sprite and >=4 variants
actually painted; path/water/bed variety; grass->path, grass->water and grass->bed transitions
exist AND every transition tile matches its recomputed neighbour mask (catches an orientation
bug); decals present, sparse, inside their grammar bucket; props render env art with UNCHANGED
world footprints (rect/PPU, checked against 1.00x1.00 tree/rock, 1.00x0.50 mound/bridge,
1.28x1.28 nest, 2.56x5.12 fence) and mound colliders still 0.7.
DETERMINISM: every painted ground/water cell must equal the library's pure derivation, and the
derivation must answer identically on two calls - since it is a hash of the cell coordinate and
nothing else, that IS the "same cell, same variant across two scene builds" guarantee, provable
without rebuilding. Same forward check on every painted decal.
Art absent on disk -> the case proves the flat fallback instead; art present but unwired ->
it fails loudly with the exact menu items to run.

REGRESSION SAFETY - walkability is computed by OverworldMap from tile PRESENCE, never identity,
so swapping one walkable tile asset for another cannot move a cell; the obstacle layer, mound
picking, stream carving and connectivity healing are untouched; the decal Tilemap is decorative
and OverworldMap never consults it. StreamsConnectivity / PathfindingAnywhere /
TownAvoidsMoundAndStream / BrachioTreeShake / AnkyRockSmash / mound taps all keep their
contract.

VERIFICATION DONE - both assemblies compiled clean with Unity 6000.0.61f1's own Roslyn against
the project's real reference set (Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-Editor); hash distribution
and decal densities validated by simulation. NOT run: the Unity editor, the integration suite,
git (per ticket rules).

NEXT (needs a human in Unity): DinoDigger/Import Generated Art -> DinoDigger/Build Main Scene ->
DinoDigger/Run Integration Tests (double-green gate). Concurrency note: another agent is
mid-edit in Dig/ + GameConfig/GameEnums; my GameConfig change is an append-only ENV region and
Dig/ was not touched.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH FILING: tree/rock VARIANT painting (gingko, conifer, mossy rock) and the
tree_gingko_shake pose are wired into the library but unused - painting them would need the
tree/rock tap contract to move off single-tile identity first.

FILES: Assets/Scripts/Config/EnvDressing.cs (new), Config/PlaceholderLibrary.cs,
Config/GameConfig.cs (ENV region), Overworld/OverworldMap.cs (decal layer + Test hooks),
Editor/GeneratedArtImporter.cs, Editor/SceneBuilder.cs, Editor/WebGLBuilder.cs,
Testing/IntegrationTestCasesEnv.cs (new), Testing/IntegrationTestCases.cs (1 line).

title: ENV art: full Jurassic-earth asset set (plates, transitions, decals, trees, rocks, bridges, fences, mounds)

comments.text:
ENV art set COMPLETE. Generator: Tools/generate_env.py (produces Assets/Art/Generated/env/).
Contact sheet (the review artifact): Assets/Art/Generated/env/contact_sheet.png
  3260x3804 - dressed 14x11 scene using the real baked tiles + backhoe + dino on top
  (answers the pitch's tap-language question), over a LABELLED catalogue of all 117
  shipped sprites. Per-group audit sheets: env/verify_*.png (10 sheets, every file shown).

MANIFEST - 117 shipped sprites (all <=256px) + 4 pipeline-master plates (never ship)
  ground/  tile_grass_00..15, tile_path_00..15, tile_water_00..15   256x128  (48)
           tile_bed_00..03                                          256x128   (4)
           edge_grass_path_1..15, edge_grass_water_1..15,
           edge_grass_bed_1..15                                     256x128  (45)
           plate_{grass,path,water,bed}.png  1024^2  MASTERS, not shipped
  decal/   fern moss footprints stones lily lily_blossom clover pebbles  <=256 (8)
  prop/    tree_cycad tree_gingko tree_conifer tree_gingko_shake      256x256
           rock_boulder rock_mossy                                   256x256
           mound                                                     256x128  (7)
  decor/   bridge_a bridge_b  256x128 | fence_x fence_y  256x512 | nest 256x256 (5)
           plate_stone.png  1024^2  MASTER, not shipped

OLD -> NEW WORLD SIZE (verified against the actual Placeholder sprites + .meta PPU).
World size == px/PPU is PRESERVED EXACTLY on every replacement, so no collider, cell
pitch or spawn rect needs retuning - the importer ticket only has to set the new PPU:
  tile_grass|path|water 128x64  @128 = 1.000x0.500 -> tile_*_NN     256x128 @256  SAME
  tile_bridge           128x64  @128 = 1.000x0.500 -> bridge_a|b    256x128 @256  SAME
  tile_mound            128x64  @128 = 1.000x0.500 -> mound         256x128 @256  SAME
  tile_tree             128x128 @128 = 1.000x1.000 -> tree_*        256x256 @256  SAME
  tile_rock             128x128 @128 = 1.000x1.000 -> rock_*        256x256 @256  SAME
  nest_base             128x128 @100 = 1.280x1.280 -> nest          256x256 @200  SAME
  Kenney fenceLow_E|N   256x512 @100 = 2.560x5.120 -> fence_x|y     256x512 @100  SAME
  fence_x/y are byte-compatible drop-ins: art composited into the same 256x512 canvas
  at the same alpha bbox (_E x0..133 y315..450, _N x0..133 y377..511), re-measured from
  the shipped Kenney PNGs, so SceneBuilder's "scale to bounds.size.x == 1 cell" is
  untouched. Decals ship trimmed; size them by world WIDTH (DECAL_WORLD_W in the script).
  NEW, no predecessor: 45 transition tiles, tile_bed_*, tree_gingko_shake, 8 decals.

STYLE VERIFICATION - every one of the 117 files inspected on the verify sheets:
  R1 outlines: props (7) carry the thick actor-weight black outline; ALL ground (97),
    decals (8) and bridge+fence (4) carry none. nest is the one deliberate exception -
    it is outlined (it is an interaction target) but filed under decor/.
  R2 quiet pass: applied in-pipeline to every plate BEFORE slicing, and to decals and
    decor. Props deliberately NOT quieted - that energy gap is the tap language.
  R3/R4/R5/R6: big soft shapes, decal grammar honoured by the scene composer, no
    lava/fire/cracks anywhere, biome means pinned to the shipped flat tile colours.
  No faces, no eyes, no text/letters/numbers/watermarks in any asset.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE BAKE (both now documented as scars in the script):
  1. ACCENT REPEAT. All 45 edge tiles derive from ONE base + ONE over square, hardcoded
     to block (1,1). That block held a PEBBLE on the path plate and a whole LILY PAD on
     the water plate, so those were reproduced pixel-identically in all 15 grass->path
     and all 15 grass->water tiles - the obvious repeat rule 3 bans, and the lily also
     broke rule 4. Fixed by scoring every block's high-frequency energy (p99.5 of
     |luma - blur9|, which finds small sharp accents that plain variance misses under
     the soft gradients) and taking the calmest: EDGE_BLOCK grass(1,1) path(0,2)
     water(3,1). Water score went 27.0 -> 12.0.
  2. BLANK BRIDGE. Stone slabs are ~350px on a 1024 plate, so the hardcoded (2,2) crop
     landed entirely inside one slab and baked out as a featureless grey diamond. Now
     takes the two BUSIEST blocks, (0,2) and (2,3): parallel grout runs and a Y-junction,
     visibly different from each other.

GENS / RETRIES / COST
  Prior (killed) session: 16 gens, all 16 raws landed in Tools/raw/env_*.png and were
    already paid for - nothing was re-generated. It had only baked `ground`, and even
    that ran before the bed plate landed. Everything else was un-sliced on disk.
  This session: audited disk vs the required set, sliced/baked ALL paid raws (122 files
    from the 16 existing raws, $0), then 1 gen + 0 retries.
  The 1 gen: env_fence REGEN. v1 came back as a loose watercolour SKETCH - scratchy
    dark-brown strokes for wood grain, i.e. line art on an asset class that must have
    none, and the wrong texture family next to the flat cel bridge/ground. Root cause:
    "soft painterly + no outlines" alone reads to the model as "sketch"; it needs a
    POSITIVE flat-fill instruction. Added the anti-sketch clause to DECOR_STYLE and it
    came back first-take as clean flat cel driftwood, correct mirroring, moss tuft kept.
  COST this session: $0.0388 (measured as an OpenRouter balance delta). Budget was $2.
  Ticket total ~ $0.66 (17 gens @ ~$0.039, gemini-2.5-flash-image). Estimate was $1.50.
  OpenRouter monthly limit remaining at close: $29.44.

import, no .meta files written for the new PNGs, nothing committed. Unity will generate

title: Tuggy the tugboat — duckling parade tow (BUILD, redesigned to amplify duck-catch)
description: Greg overrides the cut: Tuggy ships. Redesign so he amplifies the stream's duck-catch joy instead of cannibalizing it (the eval's concern): Tuggy chugs the longest stream on a slow loop; tap him -> happy toot + he tows a lily-pad line of 2-3 EXTRA ducklings behind him for a while — MORE catchable ducks, not fewer (each still flies off and pays like a normal duck when caught). No dino boarding/ferrying (avoids DinoController pathing risk entirely — he's a stream-bound spectacle+spawner like DuckController, not a transport). Found dormant moored at a stream bank, mossy-sleeper wake pattern. Cooldown between toots. Art: concept exists (tuggy_tugboat.png); needs stream sprite (2 facings or mirror), tow-line duckling art reuses existing duck, dormant state. Case: TuggyTowsDucklings (tap toots + spawns catchable ducklings, catches pay normally, cooldown holds, buddies/backhoe unaffected).
close_reason:
BUILT to Greg's duckling-parade redesign — the version that AMPLIFIES the duck-catch instead of cannibalising it.

TUGGY: arrives dormant moored at the head of the LONGEST stream course, earned by the child CATCHING THEIR FIRST DUCK (the duck-amplifier must never arrive before the ducks). Awake he chugs a forever-loop along that course at GameConfig.TuggyChugSpeed (0.32 u/s vs a duck's 0.5) using the same cell-to-cell walk a drifting Duck uses — including the under-bridge alpha fade — but turning around at each end instead of despawning. Mechanically a bigger, slower duck, exactly as briefed. NO dino boarding, so not one new state landed in DinoController.

TOOT: tap -> honk + bob + smokestack puff, and TuggyDucklingsMin..Max (2-3) ducklings drop onto the water one cell apart, each on a lily pad. They are REAL Ducks from DuckController via the new SpawnEscortDuck — same drift, same tap-to-catch, same quack + fly-off + fruit-or-treasure reward. Crucially they are tracked in a SEPARATE _escorts list, so they do NOT count against the ambient MaxAlive cap: a toot leaves the stream with strictly MORE to catch, which is the entire point. Spacing the entry cells matters — a line dropped on one cell would stay perfectly stacked forever and read as a single duck. Cooldown TuggyCooldownSeconds (40s); a cooling-down tap still gets a wobble.

ONE-CELL STREAM, NO COLLIDER FIGHTS: verified how ducks share a stream today — every water actor is a TRIGGER collider and the project has no Rigidbody2D anywhere, so nothing pushes anything and two ducks already simply overlap. The only real question an overlap raises is which one a TAP means, and that is now settled by construction: GameManager.TappableRank gained MachineFriend at rank 3 (between dino 2 and pickup 4), so DUCK (1) always out-ranks the boat. The fleeting catchable thing wins the tap; the big steady boat underneath never steals it — precisely the ambiguity the roster eval said a tugboat would create.

Case TuggyTowsDucklings proves: absent until the first catch, moored dormant + repeatedly glinting on the verified-longest course, first tap wakes it, a toot tows 2-3 ducklings onto the water while the AMBIENT duck count is untouched, a duckling genuinely overlapping Tuggy still wins its own tap and is caught normally, the cooldown holds a second toot while still answering the tap, and a refill re-arms it. (Overlap asserted here rather than by editing the shared TapPriorityOverlap case.)

title: Sprinkles the watering bot — tap-to-spray instant ripen (REDESIGNED per eval)
description: Lives at the berry garden; found dormant, tap wakes. Redesign per eval: NOT a growth-rate buff (invisible 25s timer) — tap Sprinkles and it trundles to the nearest unripe BerrySprout and sprays: instant Ripen() with sparkle payoff. Wordless belly-tank cooldown (visible fill level, refills over time). Art: concept exists; needs overworld sprite + spray anim + dormant state. Case: SprinklesRipensOnTap (ripen fires, cooldown blocks immediate repeat, refill re-enables).
close_reason:
BUILT to the REDESIGN, not the bible's spec.

SPRINKLES: arrives dormant at the berry-garden edge, earned by the child HARVESTING their first berry (the garden's only player verb — a sprout ripening on its 25s timer is nobody's doing, so a harvest is the honest 'the child has engaged this loop' signal). Placement is sampled inside the reserved garden rect (so a dig mound can never respawn on it — that rect is exactly what SpawnManager excludes) while maximising distance from the sprouts, preferring >=0.95u so it never covers a sprout's own tap target.

AWAKE: tap -> trundles at SprinklesTrundleSpeed to the NEAREST unripe sprout, stands beside it (not on it, so the arc is visible), sprays a three-puff sparkling arc, and the sprout ripens INSTANTLY. New public BerrySprout.WaterNow() routes through the same private Ripen() the timer uses, so a watered sprout is indistinguishable from a naturally ripened one — same swell tween, same sparkle, same harvest. NOT a growth-rate buff: cause and effect with nothing in between, which was the eval's whole complaint.

BELLY TANK: SprinklesTankCharges (3) sprays drawn as a visible fill bar, sipping one charge back every SprinklesRechargeSeconds (45s). IsReady is overridden to require water AND a thirsty sprout — burning a charge on an all-ripe garden would read to a child as the machine breaking. Either failure routes to the sad-cute empty-gurgle: the base wobble plus a hollow sideways slosh, so 'I'm out' reads differently from 'here you go' and a tap is never ignored.

Case SprinklesRipensOnTap proves: absent until the first harvest, arrives dormant + repeatedly glinting inside the garden rect and clear of every sprout, first tap wakes it with a full tank, a tap spends a charge and trundles it to a genuinely unripe sprout which then IS ripe, an empty tank gurgles instead of spraying and is drawn empty, and one recharge period restores a charge and re-arms the spray.

title: Glow the lantern bot — dig deep-layer companion (BUILD)
description: Found dormant behind a dirt tile in the first dark stratum (D3a depth layers); tap wakes it: belly lens lights adjacent tiles and faintly reveals buried outlines one tile ahead, turning dig taps into informed choices. Ships with/inside D3a as the pilot machine. Art: concept exists (glow_lantern_bot.png); needs in-dig sprite (side view, ~1 facing) + dormant mossy state + wake blink anim frames. Case: GlowRevealsAdjacent.
close_reason:
GLOW THE LANTERN BOT shipped — the pilot machine-character, and the first mossy sleeper that lives inside the dig.

It is an ordinary MachineFriend (GlowBot : MachineFriend), so it inherits every discipline that base enforces: state-derived visuals, resting-scale-safe wobbles, null-tolerant art, an answer to every tap in every state, and a woken flag persisted the instant it is set. MachineKind gained Glow (save id 'glow'); MachineFriendController keeps its gate + woken flag and its persistence but deliberately does NOT place it (IsOverworldMachine) — the dig site builds it — so a lantern the child has not met can never park itself in the one-discovery-at-a-time pacing guard and hold up an overworld friend.

Arc: GATE = reaching layer 2 (GameManager.NotifyDeepDigLayer -> MachineFriendController.NotifyDeepDigReached, tripped by the descent itself). Dormant behind a random layer-2 tile, rendered BEHIND the dirt with its collider off, running the base class's own arrival beacon so all the child sees is a glint out of the wall. The tile coming away (any path — bite, cascade, mushroom fling, geode) reveals it and it stretches; one tap wakes it and it hops to the pit edge, forever.

Awake in the dark, its belly beam raises the ALPHA FLOOR under buried outlines: the 3x3 around the deepest uncleared cell at DigGlowPeekAlpha, plus a 3-cell cone one tile AHEAD of every cracked tile pointing at the beam, at DigGlowConePeekAlpha. Floors are released before each sweep, so the beam can move without slowly revealing the whole board, and MAX-combined with the crack curve so the lamp can never dim a hint the child earned. It writes nothing but alpha — no damage, no hardness, no collection — so a lit tile is exactly as much digging as an unlit one: the lamp sells information, never progress. It follows between layers (re-perched by RefreshGlow on every rebuild) and on the bright surface layer dims to a night-light and lights nothing.

Art: placeholder (star-particle blob under a lantern tint) — the ~5-6 gens the roster eval sized are in the follow-up bead DinoDigger-hoy.

Files: Assets/Scripts/Dig/DigGlow.cs + GlowBot.cs (new), MachineFriend/MachineFriendController (kind, gate, IsGated/IsWoken), GameManager.Machines/NotifyDeepDigLayer, GameConfig glow block. Hooks: TestGlow/TestGlowAwake/TestGlowRow/Col/TestGlowSweeps/TestGlowRevealed/TestGlowLitCells/TestGlowLits/TestWakeGlow/TestGlowBeamCell, GlowBot.TestFlares/TestStretches/TestCovered, static pin TestSuppressGlow (cleared by the runner backstop). Case: GlowRevealsAdjacent.

title: Doodle the music-box bot — plaza dance parties (BUILD)
description: Lives at the town plaza (near Fossil Fountain); found dormant, tap wakes; thereafter tapping Doodle cranks it: nearby residents gather and each plays its existing DanceType anim as a repeatable chorus (parade is one-shot; this is the repeatable version — amplification per eval). Cooldown so it can't strobe. Art: concept exists; needs overworld sprite + crank anim frames + dormant state. Case: DoodleDanceParty (residents dance, buddies unaffected unless adjacent, cooldown honored).
close_reason:
BUILT. Doodle the music-box bot ships in the plaza.

SHARED PATTERN: new MachineFriend base component (Assets/Scripts/Overworld/MachineFriend.cs) — dormant/awake states, a charge/gauge cooldown drawn as a belly bar, the come-look arrival beacon, RestingScale-safe jiggles, state-derived visibility re-derived every LateUpdate (the hat-overlay lesson), null-tolerant art, and Test* hooks. Three thin subclasses + MachineFriendController (arrival gates, pacing queue, placement, persistence).

DOODLE: arrives dormant near the Fossil Fountain plot once >=1 building is finished. Placement is SAMPLED, not hardcoded — rings of candidates around TownArea.PlotWorld(last) scored by distance to the nearest plot, preferring >=1.7u clearance (a building's tap box is ~1.1u half-width, so Doodle's own 0.55u touch target stays fully outside it) and falling back to the roomiest spot above 0.85u. A town re-layout can never bury him.

AWAKE: tap -> crank child sprite spins three turns, music-note particles puff, and up to GameConfig.DoodleMaxDancers (4) nearby residents are gathered with the shipped WalkTo travel, then each plays its own species DanceType animation on a 1.15s beat for DoodlePartySeconds (6s) before drifting home on their normal resident behaviour. Cooldown DoodleCooldownSeconds (20s) with the visible dial; a cooling-down tap still gets a wobble + gurgle, never nothing.

CONSTRUCTION ALWAYS WINS, structurally: dancers come from the new GameManager.MachineAcquireDancers, which is TownAcquireRecessGoers' eligibility rule verbatim (non-buddy, non-busy, non-seller, not the ceremony baby) plus a proximity test — DinoController.IsBusy already covers working AND commuting, so a builder is never offered. A dancer drafted mid-song is simply taken (GoWork refuses nothing) and the party drops it on its next beat. The party holds no lock and claims nothing.

Case DoodleDanceParty in IntegrationTestCasesMachines.cs proves: absent before any building finishes, arrives dormant + repeatedly glinting and clear of every plot, first tap wakes it (moss off, eye on, dial shown), a crank gathers residents and produces real dance beats, no buddy is ever taken, the cooldown blocks a repeat but still answers the tap, and a refill re-arms it.

title: Dino anim/pose audit: limb count must be constant across frames — extra arms appearing
description: Greg: some dino poses gain limbs between frames — two arms become four, four become six (img2img stride/stage frames hallucinating extra limbs). Audit EVERY sprite pose set: 9 species x stages x 8 facings x {idle, walkA, walkB} — limb count and placement must be constant within each facing's frame set. Composite contact sheets per facing (idle|walkA|walkB side by side), visually review all, list offenders, regenerate bad frames with an explicit limb-freeze clause (same pattern as the neck/wing freezes in SPECIES_STRIDE_FREEZE), re-slice with union-box alignment, re-verify. Also bake the limb-freeze clause into stride_prompt/stage_transform_prompt permanently so future gens can't regress.
close_reason:
Audited all 135 pose sets (9 species x 3 stages x 5 generated facings; SW/W/NW are slicer mirrors of SE/E/NE so they inherit every fix). ~83 frames had anatomy changes between idle and walk.

Root cause: STRIDE_TRANSFORM described a two-legged step, which has no valid reading for a reference drawn on all fours -- the model reared quadrupeds up and redrew their front legs as arms (0 arms -> 2 arms), and in brachiosaurus/walkB_S grew a genuine third hind leg (5 limbs vs the idle's 4).

Pipeline fixed permanently in Tools/generate_sprites.py: LIMB_FREEZE (on both stride_prompt and stage_transform_prompt) + QUADRUPED_STAGES/QUAD_STRIDE_TRANSFORM/QUAD_STANCE_FREEZE (stage-aware -- brachiosaurus baby is bipedal, its adult and kid are not).

Worst 60 frames regenerated + re-sliced (~$2.31, 0 failures). Verified frame-by-frame: quadrupeds walk on four clawed feet, ankylosaurus keeps its tail club, pteranodon's wings stay folded, velociraptor's tail stays on the correct side, trex kid walkB_NE no longer drifts camera angle.

Remaining ~23 frames (baby stages + a few tails) -> DinoDigger-awr. Also noticed: triceratops has NO walk frames at all despite triceratops_strides being in the manifest -- worth its own ticket.

title: Dig arm V2: re-evaluate backhoe art/animation — proportionate alternative, toggleable, non-destructive
description: Greg: the dig-mode arm looks giant compared to the vehicle and low quality. Build an ALTERNATIVE (V2) that can be tested separately: new art in Assets/Art/Generated/digarm2/, config/demo toggle to switch versions at runtime, current V1 untouched and remains default until V2 is approved by eye. Re-evaluate proportions (arm:vehicle scale), silhouette quality, joint articulation, and animation feel (dig bite arc).
close_reason: V2 built, additive, behind GameConfig.DigArmVersion (default V1) + live demo toggle DinoDigger/Demo/Dig Arm V2 On|Off. CRITIQUE (measured from shipped V1 art): boom drawn 1.80 world units deep over its 3.4u pin span (1:1.9, a slab); base pin boss ~1.65u with a 1.37u pin hole - wider than a whole dirt tile - while the entire vehicle is 2.4u tall, so the arm out-masses its own machine. Quality: 1.2-1.7 percent of visible pixels carry magenta chroma-key fringe (purple halo); elbow mates a small round boom-tip boss to a big hexagonal stick plate; the 0.72u bucket is smaller than the elbow knuckle (inverted mass hierarchy). DESIGN: option (a) - whole backhoe (existing digbody, unchanged staging) anchors the scale; arm rebuilt slim (boom 1:8 strip ~0.46u, stick ~0.54u, SAME-diameter elbow bosses = one clean knuckle); bucket grows to 1.0u so mass reads body > bucket > arm. Bone lengths/IK/limits/bite timing are V1's untouched (reach to the deepest row is physics, not art) - V2 is a pure sprite remount through the same AssignSegmentPins/AssignBucket math, safe to flip mid-bite. Art: Tools/generate_digarm2.py, 4 gens ~USD 0.16, sliced to Assets/Art/Generated/digarm2/ with measured pins in pins.json. Test: DigArmV2Swaps (live V1->V2->V1 mid-dig, bites resolve in all phases). NOTE: run DinoDigger/Import Generated Art once to wire Boom2/Stick2/Bucket2 into the library, else the rig stays safely on V1.

comments.author: Greg Back
comments.text:
GATE FIX — CelebrationNoConsoleErrors pass-then-fail-twice diagnosed.

MECHANISM (my case's bug, amplified by cross-run save residue — not randomness):
The case waited on 'town.TestBuilderCount >= 2 && AllBuildersWorking(town)' while running the build at TownSecondsPerBuildState=0.25. A whole building is 4 x 0.25 = 1.0 work-second and ONE Big builder banks 2.5 work/s, so the FIRST builder to clock in can top the building out ~0.4s later — before the second finishes its commute. FinishSite then clears _builders, so 'all builders working' can NEVER become true and the wait burns its full 40s: exactly the reported 'the crew never all clocked in at the site (commute wedged?)'.

WHY RUN 1 PASSED AND RUNS 2-3 DID NOT: the case was the only town case that neither zeroed the wallet nor pinned TestSuspendBuilds during setup. The save file outlives play mode (GameManager.OnDestroy -> SaveNow on exit), so run N+1 boots holding run N's banked treasure, and the always-on town builder auto-spends it. With the accelerated pacing already set, ground broke during the case's own setup frames — before it had funded anything and while the residents were still being placed — which widened the arrival spread between the two builders and flipped the race from 'both arrive together' (run 1, near-empty inherited wallet) to 'one arrives, building finishes, crew cleared' (runs 2-3, fat inherited wallet).

TIMEOUT/FINALLY HOLE: checked and NOT open. IntegrationTestRunner.RunCase disposes every enumerator left on the stack after a timeout/failure, and Dispose() on a C# iterator suspended inside a try runs its finally — so case config restores do execute on timeout. Ruled out.

FIXES, at three layers:
1. CASE (root cause): pin TownController.TestSuspendBuilds through setup, zero the wallet, fund EXACTLY TownBuildingPrice(0) and only then release the pin — so the case drives one build on one plot regardless of inherited state, and the wallet drains to 0 so no second site can break ground behind the celebration. Crew is now snapshotted AS DRAFTED (TestBuilderCount >= 2, which is deterministic on the first tick after break-ground, long before anyone can walk there) instead of waiting for all-working. That is also the BETTER walk-home check: it includes a builder recalled MID-COMMUTE, which is precisely what the stranded-builder guard is about.
2. RUNNER (residue class): RestoreConfig now also re-asserts the town knobs after every case — TownSecondsPerBuildState, SnackWorkSeconds, TownCheerMultiplier/Seconds, RecessSeconds, TownVisitIntervalSeconds/BeatSeconds, TownMaxVisits — snapshotted at suite start. GameConfig is a ScriptableObject ASSET, so a runtime write sticks for the whole editor session; one missed restore would silently re-tune every later case and every later run.
3. RUNNER (cross-run channel): the suite now starts every run BROKE (Save.Data.TreasureCount = 0 once, after boot). That is the one inherited save field that changes behaviour on its own — dinos and town progress are already wiped per case by TestReset — and it makes a suite run reproducible instead of a function of the day's history.

No new statics were introduced by Phase 3 (cheer/celebration state is per-TownController instance and cleared by TestResetTown); the only new static-ish surface is the two new GameConfig fields, now covered by the backstop. Both assemblies recompile clean under Unity 6000.0.61f1 Roslyn.

title: Backhoe pathfinding robustness: any tap = guaranteed route
description: User: 'anywhere player presses, pathfinding should bring them there around rocks/streams/etc — currently takes too much manual clicking.' Likely: stall watchdog honk-gives-up at narrow 1-cell bridges/concave banks; LOS corner-cutting clips water corners; NearestWalkable radius too small for far-water taps. Fix: replan (re-run BFS) on stall instead of giving up (honk only when BFS itself fails); corridor-width LOS (parallel offset samples) so corner cuts never clip obstacles; hug cell centers through 1-cell passages; extend unwalkable-tap clamping. Test: PathfindingAnywhere — 20 random walkable targets across the island incl. across streams/pond, assert arrival within generous timeout, zero give-ups.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Greg Back
comments.text:
Fixed. Root causes: (1) stall watchdog called GiveUp->honk after 1.2s of no progress with no attempt to re-route; (2) LOS corner-cutting (SmoothWaypoints + AdvanceByLineOfSight) sampled only the centerline at 0.25 steps, so a straight shortcut could graze a water/obstacle corner between two walkable cells and wedge the follower; (3) waypoint-arrival threshold was a fixed ~2x arrive distance, so the backhoe cut corners early and clipped the far bank of 1-cell bridges; (4) NearestWalkable ring (r<=8) returned found=false for taps deep in water, making FindPath honk instead of driving to the near shore.

Design:
- REPLAN, never quit: stall watchdog and fully-blocked frame now call TryReplan() (re-run FindPath from the current position toward the same goal). Only honk when FindPath itself returns false, or after MaxReplans=5 replans per journey. _replans resets per SetDestination.
- Corridor-width LOS: new OverworldMap.HasCorridorLineOfSight samples 3 parallel lines (center +/- 0.3 world units perpendicular) and requires all walkable. Used by BOTH SmoothWaypoints and AdvanceByLineOfSight. Through a 1-cell bridge the offset samples land in the flanking water so it fails on purpose -> follower falls back to raw cell-center waypoints (hugs the bridge center).
- Narrow-passage threading: OverworldMap.IsCorridorCell detects a cell pinched by unwalkable cells on both sides of one axis; BackhoeController tightens the waypoint-advance threshold from ~2x to ~1x arrive distance when the current/next waypoint is a corridor.
- Far-water clamp: new NearestWalkable(world, towardFallback, out found) overload; if the ring fails it marches from the tap toward the mover and returns the first walkable cell (the near shore). FindPath uses it, passing fromWorld. A deep pond tap now drives to shore instead of no-op.
- Facing smoother untouched.

Test hook: BackhoeController.TestGiveUpCount (internal) counts honk-give-ups (initial FindPath fail + GiveUp).

Test: new Case_PathfindingAnywhere (Testing/IntegrationTestCases.cs, registered after RoamTapToMove, 120s). Seeds System.Random(0xD1D0), Fisher-Yates over all walkable cells, greedily picks 18 targets >=6 cells apart and >=6 from start (asserts span >=24x24). MoveTo each; asserts arrival on the exact target cell, walkable, and TestGiveUpCount stays at baseline (zero give-ups). Then parks far from the pond and routes a move AT a deep interior pond cell, asserting near-shore clamp (walkable, != water cell, moved >0.25 closer, no give-up).

Files changed: Assets/Scripts/Overworld/BackhoeController.cs, Assets/Scripts/Overworld/OverworldMap.cs, Assets/Scripts/Testing/IntegrationTestCases.cs. Did not touch SceneBuilder/StreamNetwork/DuckController or any other locked lane.

comments.author: Greg Back
comments.text: Fixed. Reworked stream carving in SceneBuilder from a biased random walk (which dead-ended and fragmented) to A* (AStarStream): each of 3 ribbons is laid as ONE unbroken 4-connected route from a coastal grass source to the pond. A* routes AROUND trees/rocks/meadow/start-clearing (RoutableForStream excludes them) and NEVER erases them; a path band it must cross is stamped 'B' (bridge) at a stiff cost so crossings stay rare and perpendicular. Courses are ordered coast->pond and store ALL cells (incl. bridged ones); walkability comes from the tilemap, so the mandatory EnsureStreamConnectivity healer still bridges ('S'->'B') any stream-cut region without breaking course continuity (the bridged cell was already in its course). D3b MEGA-FOSSIL SITES shipped. A (re)rolling mound can come up skull-marked (GameConfig.DigMegaFossilChance, plus PITY: guaranteed within DigMegaFossilPityMounds mounds while the board has an incomplete skeleton and no mega has been met this session). The mark is made in the OVERWORLD — the child chooses to accept the promise — and reuses the pit's own skull bone sprite as the marker overlay.

Digging it out completes that species in one sitting.

Two rules keep it from becoming a way to LOSE a skeleton: no ladder is ever offered on a mega site (a depth rebuild would take the un-dug bones with it), and the round does not end when the loot runs out — it ends when the bones are out (CollectIfBuried + MaybeFinishMegaRound).

PERSISTENCE, explicitly NOT required and NOT added: the mega flag is session state on the live mound. An un-dug mound stays in the world exactly like any other mound; a restart re-rolls flavours and the pity counter starts again in the child's favour, which costs nothing because the bones a mega site would bury are still the bones their board is missing. Documented in DigMegaFossil.cs and DigMound.IsMegaFossil.

title: D3c: Toy roster expansion — water pockets, dig critters, gem veins, bouncy mushrooms
description: Water pocket: gushes down the column washing tiles, floats buried items up. Critter: glowbug scurries tile-to-tile, chase-tap for giggle+coin. Gem vein: spark travels connected vein popping segments domino-style. Mushroom: scoop boings off, flings dirt clearing random neighbors. All join the D1c roller. Cases: WaterPocketWashes, CritterCatchable.
notes: Gate run 1 fix (WaterPocketWashes, 'the gush DESTROYED a tile'): WashSoft never destroyed anything — it floors at one remaining hit — but the gush's OWN collapse did. The column above falls into the hole the pocket left and lands on the tile just softened, and a landing crack on a 1-hit tile completes it, so the water was digging for the child. Fixed engine-side: DirtTile gains _washed/IsWashed (set by WashSoft, spent by the first real Damage(), cleared by SetKind) and ApplyLandingCracks now skips a washed victim — the same exemption, with the same reasoning, that crystals and the surprise pocket already have. Softening is a gift, never a theft: the child always gets the final tap. Float path audited: it moves the _buried entry and the peek together and destroys nothing. Case now also asserts IsWashed and that one bite finishes what the water started.
close_reason:
D3c TOY ROSTER EXPANSION shipped — four new toys, all in the featured-toy roller (now 8 entries, weights 3/2/2/3/2/2/2/2; a stale 4-entry config asset still rolls the new ones via DigPrimaryToyWeight's fallback) AND as secondary rolls, both taking the depth chance bonus.

WATER POCKET (DigTileKind.Water, 1 hit): bursts at the ClearTile chokepoint, so any path that clears it gushes. Logic is synchronous (whole column washed to one remaining hit via DirtTile.WashSoft — DIRT only, a toy's own promise is never rewritten; buried loot floated one row up, walked top-down so nothing moves twice, the _buried map and the peek moved together); only the splash is staggered over DigWaterGushSeconds. The float is relative to the collapse that follows, which is exactly the against-gravity read.
DIG CRITTER (DigCritter, not a tile at all): rolls out of a cleared tile (DigCritterChance, capped at DigCritterMax), scurries every ~1.5s, tap = giggle + coins + despawn, burrows away after ~10s uncaught. BLOCKS NOTHING by construction: not in _grid/_tiles, gates nothing, tiny collider, dies with the layer. Tap priority -2 (above DirtTile) so a catch is possible at all; the ladder is -1 and stands in an EMPTY cell so it steals nothing.
GEM VEIN (DigTileKind.Vein, 1 hit): 3-5 connected cells grown as a snaking WALK (tip-extension, unlike the crystal blob). A hit at either end sparks the whole run with a 0.12s per-segment stagger and pays per segment. Built as the crystal blob's twin (flood fill, copy out of its OWN scratch lists, ForceBreak with a ring delay, clear through the normal chokepoint), so every hard case it inherits is already proven.
BOUNCY MUSHROOM (DigTileKind.Mushroom): intercepts its FIRST hit in DirtTile.Damage exactly as a geode does — no damage, a big resting-scale-safe squash, and 1-2 random neighbours flung loose through the ordinary no-settle clear + one shared settle. The second bite pops it. Whatever hit it (bucket, crew clear, landing crack) the answer is the boing, decided in one place.

Art: NO new gens — each toy borrows an existing sprite under a signature tint, every lookup null-tolerant down to plain dirt. Follow-up art bead: DinoDigger-hoy.

title: D3a: Depth layers — ladder descent, per-layer hardness/loot
description: Clear threshold reveals friendly ladder tile; tap descends to layer 2 (darker bg tint, hardness rolls +1, more crystals/rarer bones/bigger treasure). 2 layers max. Cases: LadderDescends, DeeperLayerRicher.

Gate run 1 fix (LadderDescends, double descent): the _descending flag only spanned the camera dip, and with no camera parked on the pit the dip resolves SYNCHRONOUSLY — it opened and closed inside the same call, so a second request sailed through. Replaced with state: _descendFromLayer, claimed before anything else runs, makes a descent a one-way door out of a LAYER (idempotent against a re-tap during the dip, a stray tap on a collider that outlived its Destroy, or a hook called twice). DigLadder is now consume-on-first-tap (collider off immediately, beacon stopped) since Destroy only takes effect at end of frame. _descents/_layer/_descending/_descendFromLayer now reset per SITE (ResetDepthForNewSite, called from Open/Close/TestBuildThemedSite/TestBuildMegaSite). Case pins DigDepthLayers=2, asserts TestMaxLayers, and now asserts idempotence directly (two extra TestDescend calls must leave TestDescents==1).

Gate run 1 fix (DeeperLayerRicher, 108 vs expected 102): the FEATURE was right, the case's formula was naive. Hardness is a DIRT rule — a toy seats its own hardness in SetKind (crystal 1, pot 2) and depth deliberately never touches it, so a whole-board sum moves with composition as well as with the bonus (the deep layer's extra crystal cluster re-seated several tiles at 1). Case split into two passes: PASS A with TestSuppressToys pinned (every tile is dirt, so deepSum == shallowSum + bonus*tiles is exact arithmetic, plus a per-tile check), PASS B with toys live asserting the rule PER KIND (dirt carries the bonus, every toy keeps its own value) alongside the per-layer feature no-repeat. New hooks: TestDirtHardnessSum, TestDirtTileCount, TestMaxLayers.

Clearing enough of a layer (GameConfig.DigLadderRevealFraction, default 0.6 — OR the layer being down to its last buried item, so the ladder is always offered before a round can end) reveals a big friendly LADDER at a clear bottom cell, speaking the game's one come-look language (sway + repeating glint, same as the surprise pocket and the mossy sleepers). title: Deflake MultiItemCollection: 30s timeout under load (1x)
description: Seen once during Phase 2 gating while two Unity editors + heavy agent load ran concurrently; passed all other runs same day. Suspect real-time budget too tight under load. Consider distance/step-proportional budget like PathfindingAnywhere got, or event-driven waits.
close_reason: Root cause was a WINDOW race, not a tight budget: the case polled for an exact instantaneous alive-pickup count, which only holds between 'every dug item landed' and 'the first egg wobbles open' (~1.2s of scaled time), AND for an exact wallet value that the always-on town builder can spend in the banking frame. Under load one frame carries up to 1s of scaled time (deltaTime clamped to maximumDeltaTime, x3 timeScale), so the poll could step straight over the window and then wait forever -> 30s timeout. Fix: track the PEAK pickup count (monotone, never decays) instead of the instantaneous one and assert peak == expected afterwards; freeze the build queue (TownController.TestSuspendBuilds) so the wallet is monotone, wait on >= and assert the exact gain; all waits bounded and named (roam 20s, batch 25s with a lazily-built failure message reporting how far it got). EnterDig's two unbounded waits also got distance-proportional budgets (LegBudget+5s) + names. Timeout 30->60s.

title: Deflake SurprisePocket: surprise fired without being cracked (1x)
description: Seen once during Phase 2 gating (2026-07-14), passed in runs before and after. Hypothesis: BigDinoHelps-style adjacent splash damage or dig-crew superpower cracked the pocket tile as a side effect of layout randomness; or timing under machine load. Deflake like DirtTileDamage: pin the layout/hardness via Test hooks or isolate the pocket tile from splash sources.
close_reason:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED after the gate run reproduced it with the crew pinned off — so my 'only a crew superpower can crack it without a tap' claim was wrong, and TestCrewCount==0 passing proved the pin engaged. Real mechanism, a genuine gameplay bug: the staggered helper cascades address tiles by GRID COORDINATE inside a delayed callback. FireGeode fires its 8-neighbour ring through Tween.After(i*0.06s) -> TileAt(r,c) -> ClearTileFully, guarded only by _open/_finished — which does NOT cover a site that CLOSES and a NEW one that OPENS inside the 0.42s (scaled) stagger window. The case does exactly that: section 3 forces kind 2 (Geode) and fires it via TestClearSurpriseTile, then ~5 frames later calls TestForceRoam (Close -> _open=false) and section 4 calls EnterDig — and because TestForceRoam does NOT consume the mound, the backhoe is still parked ON the mound it just dug, so DriveToMound arrives immediately and Open() rebuilds the grid within 1-2 frames. Timeline at 60fps/timeScale 3: ~0.25s scaled to TestForceRoam + 0.10-0.15s to the new Open = 0.35-0.40s, while the last ring callbacks are scheduled at 0.36s and 0.42s. They land on the NEW grid and crumble whatever now sits at those coordinates — roughly a 3-6%/run chance of hitting that site's untouched pocket. Frame quantisation of WaitForSeconds is what made it intermittent.
FIX (gameplay, behaviour-preserving): DigModeController._siteGeneration, bumped in BuildGrid and Close; FireGeode and HeadbuttColumn capture it and bail when it has moved on. Within one open site the generation is constant, so cascades behave exactly as before; only cross-site leakage stops. Audited every other deferred callback in the file — the Giggle/Duck coin spawns and the FX cleanups touch no tiles, and the coin spawns are deliberately left unguarded so a fast exit cannot swallow a pocket's payout.
BREADCRUMB (as requested, no reflection): ClearTileFully takes a cause string, ResolveDig tags 'player bite' / 'T-Rex adjacent clear', and CollectIfBuried records _surpriseFiredBy = cause + tile row/col + frame + site generation, exposed as internal TestSurpriseFiredBy. The 'never cracked' assertion now prints it, and the Giggle section asserts the breadcrumb reads 'player bite' so it can never be silently empty. The TestSuppressCrew pin stays as belt-and-braces.

title: Dig tile break-taps: theme-tied hardness + capped low-biased jitter
description:
The uniform DirtHealth=3 taps-per-tile is the most repetitive beat in the dig loop (Greg raised this 2026-07-19). Groundwork already exists: DirtTile._maxHealth is per-tile and RefreshSprite already maps damage proportionally across the 3 crack sprites at ANY health, so only DigModeController passes a constant 3.

Recommended design (toddler-safe): tie BASE hardness to the DigTheme (Sandy Beach soft 1-2, Meadow 2-3, Sparkle Cave crystal-hard 3-4) via a HardnessRange per DigTheme, then add mild per-tile jitter within that range, distribution weighted LOW (lots of 1-2, rare 4, never higher). The fun is the fast crumble; a stubborn tile reads as a chore for a toddler.

Deliberately NOT doing contents-tied tap counts: peek hints already telegraph contents (SetPeek shows the item from the start), so it double-signals, and gating the best loot behind the most taps inverts the toddler reward curve. Better expression of that instinct: make the BREAK MOMENT juicier for good loot (bigger crumb burst / shake / brighter chime) rather than requiring more taps. Consider as a small follow-on.

Files: Assets/Scripts/Config/GameConfig.cs (DigTheme HardnessRange), Assets/Scripts/Dig/DigModeController.cs (PlaceItems/BuildGrid per-tile roll). DirtTile needs no change. Add an integration case for the roll distribution and the crack-sprite mapping at non-3 health. Awaiting Greg go-ahead before implementing.

title: FindTappable: deterministic priority when colliders overlap
description: GameManager.FindTappable returns the first ITappable from OverlapPointAll, which is unordered. A respawned DigMound collider can clip a finished building footprint (found during Recess Time testing), so a tap in the overlap nondeterministically opens a dig instead of a party. Give FindTappable an explicit priority (dino > pickup > mound > building, or nearest-center wins) so overlapping tappables resolve predictably. Also consider keeping mound respawn points clear of building footprints in SpawnManager.
close_reason:
(1) GameManager.FindTappable now ranks every hit instead of returning the first from the unordered OverlapPointAll: DirtTile 0 > Duck 1 > Dino 2 > ItemPickup 3 > BerrySprout 4 > DigMound 5 > BuildingController 6 (unknown implementors last = old behaviour), with nearest-collider-centre as the tiebreak inside a rank. Checked all 7 ITappable implementors; order is living/interactive above ground props, and mound above building because the mound is the smaller, TRANSIENT thing a toddler aims at when the two overlap. Every existing case still resolves as before (RecessTime already taps a building-only point; MoundToDig/FruitPunch/FeedAndGrow have no overlapping tappable). Bonus: dig-tile taps can no longer resolve to a neighbouring tile.
(2) SpawnManager keeps respawns off built plots: new SetTown(town) wiring (GameManager.Awake + TestInstallTown) plus TownController.NearBuiltPlot(world, 1.2u) covering finished plots and the active site, folded into a shared CanPlace() filter. Needed because the existing exclusion is the district rect measured in CELLS while a building imports ~2.2 units wide, so a mound one cell outside the district could still clip its collider.
(3) New integration case TapPriorityOverlap (40s, 59 cases total): authors building 0 finished, FORCES the overlap by parking an active mound on the exact point where the building was the only tappable, then asserts the resolution is the mound and IDENTICAL across 11 asks, that the routed tap takes the mound branch (no recess feedback, no party), and — with the district rect temporarily cleared and the player parked far off, so no other rule can mask it — that Spawn.TestCanPlace refuses the plot and its 1.2u ring while still accepting ordinary island cells. Mound, district and save state are all restored in the finally.
Support added: GameManager.TestFindTappable, SpawnManager.TestCanPlace, BackhoeController.TestTeleport; RoutedTapOnBuilding refactored onto a shared FindBuildingOnlyPoint.

title: Flaky integration tests: FacingCorrectness, DuckCatch, PlayerControlUnaffectedByBuild
description: Three pre-existing timing-sensitive cases each flaked once across 9 suite runs during the town-persistence work (each passed on rerun): FacingCorrectness (backhoe iso-facing settle on the exact N/NE boundary), DuckCatch, and PlayerControlUnaffectedByBuild (distinct-move-target helper). All live in movement/facing code untouched by that change. Likely aggravated by the editor running unfocused (WebGL pause-when-hidden emulation per the runner comments). Worth deflaking so double-green gates stop costing extra runs.
notes: Gate follow-up (run A, 58/59): PlayerControlUnaffectedByBuild failed with 'the build vanished mid-check'. Cause of the NEW failure: the reworked bounded budgets (100s case, 40s commute wait) let the 2-Big-builder crew legitimately FINISH the building while the case was still verifying tap-move/buddy/dig — the old 45s version simply ran out of checks first. Fix: park cfg.TownSecondsPerBuildState = 1000f for the whole case (BigDinoBuildsFaster's pattern) inside a try/finally that restores it (the runner's RestoreConfig does not cover this field) and also does the TestForceRoam/TestReset teardown, so a failing assertion no longer leaves the pacing or the town dirty. Construction stays genuinely ACTIVE — ground is still broken from the wallet, the crew still commutes and works on site — the site just never reaches its final state, which is what this case wants; state progression stays covered by BuildAdvancesThroughStates and BuildingFinishesAndCelebrates. All existing assertions kept, plus the same 'site still active' invariant re-asserted after the tap-move and dig-entry phases with phase-named messages, so a future pin failure says which phase saw it vanish.
close_reason:
FacingCorrectness: each leg now teleports via new BackhoeController.TestTeleport (resets the FacingSmoother, honouring its documented teleport contract) to a fixed non-adjacent start facing, drives with a distance-proportional realtime budget (LegBudget = 6+0.5*dist, cap 20s), and re-drives up to 3x — convergence is motion-driven, never wall-clock (the smoother's deadband freezes facing while parked, so the old 'top up to 0.4s with a stationary wait' could never finish a hitch-truncated convergence). Added FacingAcceptable(): an adjacent sector passes only when the ACTUAL leg heading is inside that neighbour's 22.5+11 deg hysteresis band; 2+ sectors out still fails loudly.
